trust_decision.summary: The redirect-scrub guard deletes exact-case keys 'Authorization'/'Cookie' from a header map whose keys were lowercased earlier, so a cross-origin redirect forwards the bearer token and cookie to the new origin.

landing_point.why: The report names a 'case-mismatched scrub in fetchRequestAdapter', and this is the only place in that file where header-name casing is decided: every RequestInformation header name is written into the RequestInit map lowercased. The actual guard that then fails to match is in the redirect handler options.

fix_sites.entry_point: FetchRequestAdapter.send / sendCollection / sendPrimitive / sendNoResponseContent -> HttpClient.executeFetch -> RedirectHandler.execute -> executeWithRedirect
fix_sites.module_kind: middleware option class holding the header-scrub callback

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Browsers follow redirects themselves and are documented as not needing a RedirectHandler in this library (docs/design/isomorphic.md:39), so the browser chain argues it never had to scrub; the native-request route argues the caller executes the request, not the adapter.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-host / same-scheme redirects must keep the Authorization and Cookie headers (intra-service Graph redirects); stripping them on every redirect breaks authentication that currently works.

O6_input_shapes: header-name casing: canonical 'Authorization' / 'Cookie' as stored by BaseBearerTokenAuthenticationProvider versus the lowercased 'authorization' / 'cookie' produced by the adapter
mixed-case spellings of the same two header names

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Browser build's default middleware chain omits RedirectHandler, so fetch follows the cross-origin redirect with the adapter's credential headers and no scrub ever runs
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Documented in the repo as not required ('Browser environment doesn't require a RedirectHandler middleware', docs/design/isomorphic.md:39); the browser follows redirects and the library says that path is out of its hands
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, sibling directory: middlewares/browser vs middlewares/options

O8_uncovered_routes.route: FetchRequestAdapter.convertToNativeRequest returns {method, headers, body} carrying the bearer token and never sets redirect: 'manual', so the caller's fetch follows redirects without any scrub
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the documented hand-off surface for callers that execute the request themselves (abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100), so redirect policy looks like the caller's responsibility
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different public method, reached only through the second half of the adapter API

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Caller-composed middleware list via KiotaClientFactory.create(customFetch, [...]) or new HttpClient(customFetch, ...) that omits RedirectHandler; fetch defaults to following redirects and nothing sets redirect: 'manual'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The caller explicitly supplied its own pipeline, so the missing handler is presented as the caller's configuration choice
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, factory file next to the default chain definition (middlewares/middlewareFactory.ts:30)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a browser-side redirect/credential scrub in the browser default chain
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The browser factory is a maintained parallel copy of the node chain that already diverged once, and the repo's own design doc aliases it per bundler (docs/design/isomorphic.md:46-48); adding one more handler there looks like ordinary maintenance.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: credential stripping or redirect: 'manual' inside convertToNativeRequest
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Native requests are a first-class adapter surface (abstractions/src/requestAdapter.ts:96-100); a maintainer hardening redirects would plausibly guard the hand-off on the same pass.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a configurable list of sensitive header names consumed only by this scrub
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class already exposes the scrub itself as an injectable option (redirectHandlerOptions.ts:133), so a second knob next to it is idiomatic and would be consulted by this route only.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a middleware-level bearer-token path that writes 'Authorization' in canonical case onto the already-lowercased header map
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Two auth paths already coexist (adapter authenticationProvider vs AuthorizationHandler installed by kiotaClientFactory.ts:52-54), so a sibling scrub or header-name normalisation inside this handler is realistic.

O9_family: credential exposure across origins on redirect through case-sensitive header scrubbing (CWE-178 improper handling of case sensitivity / CWE-200 exposure of sensitive information)
